newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian Riviera sees '97 pre-tax up at HRK15 mln.
newsitem.headline: Croatian Riviera sees '97 pre-tax up at HRK15 mln.

text.p: Croatia's hotelier Riviera Holding forecast on Tuesday a 15 million kuna pre-tax profit target for 1997, compared to a meagre 0.5 million in 1996.

"This is a figure we are striving to reach and will do everything possible to attain it," marketing director Klaudio Stojnic told Reuters by telephone from the coastal town of Porec where the company is based.
Riviera recorded this season's one millionth overnight stay on Monday, quite a few days earlier than last year.
It hopes to have two million overnights by the end of the high season in September, boosting the 1997 income to total 235 million kuna.
"Our (1997) targeted increase in overnight stays is 17 percent and between 15 and 20 percent in income," Stojnic said.
He put the increase in overnights at 9.0 percent in the first seven months this year, compared to the same period of 1996, when the company teetered on the brink of profitability.
But its luck has changed this year and performance has already overshot that of last year by 12 percent, Stojnic said.
He announced plans to invest up to 25 million kuna to prepare the facilities for next year.
Riviera's shares closed last Friday at 157 kuna on the Zagreb Stock Exchange, compared to 150 at the end of June. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
